items.english: What is in the pocket?
items.target: ポケットのなかになにがありますか
items.pronunciation: poketto no naka ni nani ga arimasu ka
items.note: なか (naka) works for the inside of anything with an inside, from a pocket to a whole building.

items.english: There are also hot springs.
items.target: おんせんもあります
items.pronunciation: onsen mo arimasu
items.note: も (mo) pushes が (ga) out: a noun cannot carry both, so おんせんが becomes おんせんも.
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, second half of Nakamura's reply. The lesson's only も + あります example.

items.english: On Saturday, I'm going to Nikko with Emma-san.
items.target: どようびにエマさんとにっこうにいきます
items.pronunciation: doyōbi ni ema-san to nikkō ni ikimasu
items.note: にっこう (nikkō) is a mountain temple town about two hours north of Tokyo, a standard weekend trip.
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Nakamura's opening line, which sets up the whole lesson.

items.english: Tanaka-san is there.
items.target: たなかさんがいます
items.pronunciation: tanaka-san ga imasu
items.scene: answering who is at the information desk
items.note: が (ga) marks たなかさん as exactly the piece of information the questioner was missing.
items.reviewNote: EXERCISE 3B, the printed example answer. Elliptical, so it carries a scene.

items.english: Smith-san is there.
items.target: スミスさんがいます
items.pronunciation: sumisu-san ga imasu
items.scene: answering who is on the third floor

items.english: There is a chair in front of the desk.
items.target: つくえのまえにいすがあります
items.pronunciation: tsukue no mae ni isu ga arimasu
items.note: いす (isu) covers any chair or seat, including one on a train. A sofa is not counted as an いす: it gets its own word, ソファー (sofā).
items.reviewNote: Vocabulary job: いす appeared only as a bare WORD POWER item. Constructed.

items.english: There is a bag under the bed.
items.target: ベッドのしたにかばんがあります
items.pronunciation: beddo no shita ni kaban ga arimasu
items.note: A ベッド (beddo) is the Western-style bed of a hotel room, as opposed to a ふとん (futon), the bedding laid out on the floor in a Japanese-style room.
items.reviewNote: Vocabulary job: ベッド appeared only as a bare WORD POWER item. Constructed.

The deck teaches インフォメーション = "Information desk" as its own card, so that English is an ambiguous Production prompt; chapter 1 defines うけつけ as "Reception desk" and chapter-13-extras already uses that wording. Do not revert to match the source.

items.english: Yesterday Tanaka-san was in the meeting room.
items.target: きのうかいぎしつにたなかさんがいました
items.pronunciation: kinō kaigishitsu ni tanaka-san ga imashita
items.note: います (imasu) is for animate subjects only, so people, animals and insects. A kettle or a building in the same slot would take ありました (arimashita).
items.reviewNote: Paradigm gap: いました, the past affirmative cell of the います row. Constructed. Fixed frame shared with the いませんでした card that follows.

items.english: There is also a post office near the station.
items.target: えきのちかくにゆうびんきょくもあります
items.pronunciation: eki no chikaku ni yūbinkyoku mo arimasu
items.note: も (mo) marks the post office as an addition to something already mentioned. With ゆうびんきょくが (yūbinkyoku ga) instead, it would be presented as the first piece of news.
items.reviewNote: Particle job: the deck's only も + あります is the elliptical おんせんもあります, with no place phrase. This gives the full placeに + noun も + あります frame. Constructed.

items.english: What is there at Kamakura?
items.target: かまくらになにがありますか
items.pronunciation: kamakura ni nani ga arimasu ka
items.note: かまくら (kamakura) was Japan's capital in the 12th and 13th centuries and is an easy day trip from Tokyo.
items.reviewNote: EXERCISE 7 dialogue 1, Smith's line.

items.english: Last year there was no convenience store in front of the station.
items.target: きょねんえきのまえにコンビニがありませんでした
items.pronunciation: kyonen eki no mae ni konbini ga arimasen deshita
items.note: The past negative is ありませんでした (arimasen deshita). There is no ありませんかった: the なかった (nakatta) ending from Lesson 11 belongs to い-adjectives, not to verbs.
items.reviewNote: Paradigm gap: ありませんでした, the past negative cell of the chapter's verb table. Constructed. Same frame as the ありました card above.

items.note: あります (arimasu) is an ordinary ます-verb, so its past is built exactly like たべました (tabemashita) and いきました (ikimashita) in Lesson 8.

items.english: What is tempura?
items.target: てんぷらってなんですか
items.pronunciation: tenpura tte nan desu ka
items.note: って (tte) is a casual contraction that picks up a word you have just heard and marks it as the thing you are asking about. It stands in for は (wa) here; the formal equivalent is とはなんですか (to wa nan desu ka).
items.reviewNote: Pattern job: a second instance of the chapter's ってなんですか frame, on てんぷら from Lesson 8, so the pattern reads as a slot rather than being welded to おんせん. Constructed.

items.english: There is an electric kettle in the room.
items.target: へやにでんきポットがあります
items.pronunciation: heya ni denki potto ga arimasu
items.note: A でんきポット (denki potto) is a plug-in dispenser that keeps water hot all day, not a stovetop kettle you boil once. Hotel rooms and offices in Japan nearly always have one.
items.reviewNote: Vocabulary job: でんきポット appeared only as a bare WORD POWER item. Constructed.

items.english: There is a man at the reception desk.
items.target: うけつけにおとこのひとがいます
items.pronunciation: uketsuke ni otoko no hito ga imasu
items.note: おとこのひと (otoko no hito) is the neutral way to say 'man'; おとこ (otoko) alone can sound blunt.
items.reviewNote: EXERCISE 2B alternative 1, completed on the printed example うけつけにおんなのひとがいます. | Deliberately diverges from the book, which glosses うけつけ as "information desk" here. The deck teaches インフォメーション = "Information desk" as its own card, so that English is an ambiguous Production prompt; chapter 1 defines うけつけ as "Reception desk" and chapter-13-extras already uses that wording. Do not revert to match the source.
